# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 26 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 26 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_026_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 1 — Believe in One God

**1** First of all, believe that God is one — who created and brought all things to completion, who made all things out of nothing to exist, who contains all things and is himself alone uncontained. **2** Believe in him therefore and fear him; and fearing him, exercise self-control. Keep these things and you will cast off all wickedness from yourself and clothe yourself with every virtue of righteousness, and you will live to God if you keep this commandment.

---

### Council Notes

Mandate 1 is the theological foundation of the entire Mandates section. It is the shortest mandate — a single paragraph — but carries the greatest theological weight.

The formula "made all things out of nothing" (ek tou mē ontos) is the most explicit ex nihilo creation statement in the Shepherd (also appearing in Vision 1.1.6). This is among the earliest clear formulations of creation ex nihilo in Christian literature, predating many patristic treatments.

"Contains all things and is himself alone uncontained" — this formulation of divine transcendence/immanence is philosophically sophisticated: God is the container of all reality but cannot himself be contained by any category or space. This is resonant with both Stoic and Platonic philosophical thought, showing Hermas's Roman cultural context.

The ethical chain flowing from this theology: believe → fear → self-control → righteousness → life to God. This is the moral structure underlying all twelve mandates.
